# Moving Libraries by Intent, in Constrained Space

> ⚠️ **Not scheduled.** Recorded 2026-08-07 at the operator's direction, to be implemented only after the metadata campaign and the filename-rename feature are complete. Written now so the design is settled while the reasoning is fresh.
## The ask
*"Make Move Videos Between Libraries more useful — put all my favourites into this library, move this series, everything from these actors. Understand free disk space, and in a constrained environment shuffle files between devices to make room."*
Two separable features, and they are very different in risk. **Selection by intent is mostly built.** The shuffle is new, and it is the only genuinely dangerous part of this spec.
## ⭐ What already works — do not re-specify it
`LibraryTransferView` already shares `AssetFilterCriteria` **verbatim** with the All Assets grid, and already runs the destination's free-space check.
| Ask | Status |
| --- | --- |
| "everything from these actors" | ✅ `selectedActors` |
| "all my favourites" | ✅ `minRating` |
| by studio, tag, review status, lookup result, age at release | ✅ already filterable |
| "move this series" | ❌ **no series filter exists** — `AssetFilterCriteria` has no `videoName` dimension at all |
| a SAVED filter driving a move | ❌ Smart Collections are not reachable from the transfer screen |
## D1 — Two small gaps close most of the ask
**Series becomes a filter dimension.** `selectedSeries: Set<String>` matching `Asset.videoName`, with the same AND/OR treatment the other set filters have.
⚠️ It must be Optional or tolerantly decoded. A synthesized decoder requires a key for every non-optional property, and adding one non-optionally breaks every Smart Collection already saved — a defect caught once already by `testOlderSavedFiltersStillDecode`.
**Smart Collections become a transfer source.** A saved filter IS a stated intent; re-typing it in the transfer screen is the same decision made twice. Picking one populates the criteria, which stays editable — it seeds, it does not lock.
⭐ Together these turn *"put all my favourites into this library"* into a two-tap operation with no new transfer machinery at all.
## 🚨 D2 — Placement RULES, not one set and one destination
⭐ **Revised 2026-08-07 after the operator described the real use.** The original design assumed one wanted set moving to one destination. The actual ask is several placements at once, in both directions:
> *"Put all the videos from one studio onto the drive library and all the videos from another studio on the phone library."*
That is not a move instruction. It is a **statement of where things belong**, and the moves are derived from it.
```javascript
Rule  :=  (criteria)  →  (library)
Plan  :=  for each library: desired contents
          minus  actual contents
          =      the moves
```
⭐ **Declarative beats imperative here**, and the operator's framing is what makes it so. "Move these" has to be re-issued whenever the library changes; "these belong there" can be re-run, and a second run after adding videos does the right thing with no new instruction. It also makes the two-way case fall out naturally rather than needing its own mode.
### 🚨 Two rules can contradict each other
A video matching a rule for library A **and** a rule for library B has no defensible home. Studio and actor rules overlap constantly — one video has both.
⚠️ **Contradictions are REPORTED and the plan refuses to run**, listing the videos and the two rules that claim them. Resolving by rule order would make the outcome depend on the order the operator happened to add them, which is not a decision anyone made.
## 🚨 D2b — What may be displaced is CHOSEN, never inferred
The shuffle moves files the operator did not ask to move. Which files those are is a decision about what belongs where, and nothing in the data implies it.
**The plan therefore takes two criteria sets:**
| Set | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Wanted** | what should end up on the destination |
| **Displaceable** | what may be pushed the other way to make room |
⚠️ **Displaceable defaults to EMPTY.** With no displaceable set the tool behaves exactly as today: move what fits, report what did not. The shuffle is opt-in, and a tool that starts relocating unrelated files because a disk was full would be indefensible.
⚠️ **A placement rule beats the displaceable rule.** A video that both "belongs on the drive" and "is under 4 stars so may move" stays where it was placed — the explicit statement wins over the permissive one. Anything else would let a permission undo an instruction.
### ⭐ "May be moved at random" means permission, not randomness
The operator's phrasing — *"anything below 4 stars may be moved at random to make space"* — grants permission over a set. It does not ask for an arbitrary outcome.
⚠️ So the planner **chooses deliberately and the plan is still shown before anything moves.** Actual randomness would make the plan unreviewable and two runs of the same request incomparable.
The selection rule is **largest files first**, because it frees the required space in the fewest moves — and every move is a copy, a hash verification and a delete of a file measured in gigabytes. Fewest moves is the difference between minutes and an hour.
⚠️ Displacement stops the moment enough space exists. It is not a tidy-up; it moves the minimum that makes the placement possible.
## 🚨 D3 — The plan is computed WHOLE, shown, and persisted before anything moves
This is the difference between a feature and a way to lose a library.
1. **Compute** every step: source, destination, size, order.
2. **Show** it: N files out, M files back, peak space needed on each side, total bytes moved.
3. **Persist** it before the first copy.
4. **Execute** step by step, marking each done.
⚠️ **Persisted because it is interruptible.** A drive is unplugged, a laptop sleeps, the app is killed. Without a stored plan, a half-run shuffle is a library whose files are distributed across two volumes with no record of where anything was going — and no way to tell a completed move from an abandoned one.
⭐ Each step is already safe individually: `VideoTransferService.moveVideo` copies, verifies by SHA-256, writes metadata, and only then deletes the source. **The plan inherits that** — what it adds is knowing what to do next after an interruption.
## D4 — A file is never moved twice
A naive greedy shuffle can move a video A→B early to satisfy a constraint and B→A later to satisfy another. On files of this size that is minutes of I/O for no net change.
**The plan is validated before it is shown: every video appears at most once.** A plan that would move one twice is a planning defect, and is rejected rather than executed.
## D5 — Free space is measured with headroom, and re-checked at every step
```javascript
usable_free  =  volume_free_bytes  -  (largest_single_file * 1.1)  -  500 MB
```
⚠️ **Other processes write to these volumes.** A plan computed against a snapshot is a plan against a number that has already changed — so free space is re-measured before each step, and a step that no longer fits **pauses the run and reports** rather than failing mid-copy.
⚠️ The reserve is deliberately generous. This runs on volumes the operator has already described as constrained, and the failure mode of being slightly too optimistic is a full disk during a copy.
## 🚨 D6 — Never the last copy
At every moment of a shuffle, every video exists in at least one complete, verified location.
- A source file is deleted only after the destination copy is written **and hash-verified** — already true of `moveVideo`.
- ⚠️ A displaced file follows the same rule. Displacement is a move, not an eviction, and there is no point at which "it is being relocated" means "it is nowhere".
- A step interrupted between copy and delete leaves **two** copies. That is the correct failure: recoverable, and detectable by the existing duplicate finder.
## D7 — A plan that cannot complete never starts
If the wanted set does not fit even after every displaceable file has moved, the tool **refuses and reports the shortfall in bytes** — naming how much more would need to be freed, or how much of the wanted set would fit.
⚠️ Partial execution of an impossible plan is the worst outcome available: hours of I/O, both libraries rearranged, and the original goal still unmet.
## D8 — Removable volumes
🚨 A drive unplugged mid-run is the realistic failure here, not a theoretical one.
- Each step verifies both volumes are mounted before it begins.
- A vanished volume **pauses** the plan; it does not fail it.
- Re-attaching and re-opening the tool offers to resume from the stored plan.
- ⚠️ A resumed plan re-verifies from disk rather than trusting its own record: the operator may have moved files by hand in between, and the plan is a statement of intent, not of fact.
## Test strategy (Constitution Art. III)
- **T1** — A wanted set that fits produces a plan with no displacement, identical to today's behaviour.
- **T2** — A wanted set that does not fit, with an empty displaceable set, is REFUSED with a byte shortfall — never partially run.
- **T3** — A wanted set that fits only after displacement produces an interleaved plan, and every video appears exactly once.
- **T4** — 🚨 A plan that would move any video twice is rejected at validation.
- **T5** — Overlap between wanted and displaceable is rejected at plan time.
- **T6** — Interrupting after a copy but before a delete leaves both copies, and resume completes rather than re-copying.
- **T7** — A volume unmounted mid-plan pauses; re-attaching resumes from the correct step.
- **T8** — Free space shrinking between planning and execution pauses at the affected step rather than failing during a copy.
- **T9** — Every step's destination is hash-verified before its source is deleted (inherited, asserted again here because the plan multiplies the consequences).
- **T10** — A resumed plan re-verifies from disk, and a file the operator moved by hand does not cause a failure.
## ✅ SETTLED WITH THE OPERATOR — 2026-08-07
**1. Favourites are star ratings.** No new concept. `minRating` already expresses it, so "put my favourites on this library" is a placement rule with a rating criterion and needs nothing built.
**2. Displacement is criteria-driven, like everything else.** The operator's example — *"anything below 4 stars may be moved to make space"* — is a rating criterion, and the same filter builder expresses it. ⚠️ Still defaulting to EMPTY: the tool shuffles nothing until a rule says it may.
**3. Two libraries only.** Confirmed. ⭐ This keeps the planner a greedy pass over a known pair rather than a placement solver, and it means "the other library" is always unambiguous — which D2's rules depend on, since a rule names a destination and everything else is *the other one*.
⚠️ **A third library is refused, not approximated.** The transfer screen is already gated to a single attachment; that gate now has a stated reason rather than an incidental one.
## Superseded questions, for the record
**1. What is a "favourite"?** Today the closest thing is a star rating. If favourites should be their own concept — a flag, or a specific playlist — that is a separate decision and is worth settling before this is built, because it changes the filter rather than the transfer.
**2. Should the displaceable set have a default suggestion?** For example *"videos you have already reviewed and rated below 3"*. ⚠️ The recommendation is **no**: suggesting what to evict is a judgement about the operator's own library, and getting it wrong moves gigabytes of the wrong thing. Better an empty set and an explicit choice.
**3. More than two libraries?** The ask describes two devices. Three would make this a general placement problem, and the plan would need a solver rather than a greedy pass. The recommendation is to **build for two and refuse a third**, rather than pretend to generality nobody has asked for. — *Confirmed: two only.*
## What this spec now needs built
| Piece | Size |
| --- | --- |
| `selectedSeries` filter dimension | small — mirrors the existing set filters |
| Smart Collections reachable from the transfer screen | small — seeds existing criteria |
| Placement rules: several criteria → library pairs | medium — new model, but pure and testable |
| Contradiction detection across rules | small, and non-negotiable |
| The plan: derive moves, validate, persist, resume | 🚨 the real work, and the only dangerous part |
⭐ Worth noting how much of this is NOT transfer machinery. `moveVideo` already copies, hash-verifies, writes metadata and only then deletes; the free-space check already exists; the filter model already exists and is already shared with this screen. The new code is a planner — and a planner is a pure function over sizes and criteria, which is the most testable thing in the project.
